title: Small arterial branches leave at large angles, large branches at small angles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Small arterial branches leave at large angles, large branches at small angles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Small arterial branches come off the main stem at large angles (about 70°–90° for the smallest) and large branches at small angles, with equal branches diverging at equal angles, as Roux's rules state.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In other words, it would seem that for small branches a large angle of bifurcation, and for large branches a small one, is always the better.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Branching of arteries”. Scope: arterial branching in vertebrates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variables and directional prediction are direct and standard geometric analyses are feasible. Coverage of the smallest branches and vertebrate diversity is insufficient for the universal scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure parent and daughter diameters and branch angles in segmented arterial trees, then regress angle on relative branch caliber and test symmetry for equal daughters. A flat or reversed relationship would refute the rule.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Clinical scans favor large vessels.

Branch angle depends on organ, flow state and imaging posture.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Roux's angle rules map onto radii and bifurcation angles that public vascular reconstructions already store. A small team can fit the angle-size curve and the equal-branch case with ordinary morphometry. Failure in these large human samples would refute the rule as a general arterial fact; agreement would establish it for the beds that dominate existing open data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: At each bifurcation, measure the branch angle and the daughter-to-parent radius ratio. The claim is supported if angle declines as relative branch size increases, with the smallest side branches near 70-90 degrees and equal daughters leaving at equal angles; a flat or reversed angle-size relation would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Open trees sample humans heavily and leave most vertebrate groups unmeasured.

Angles measured from projected angiograms differ from true three-dimensional angles.
